questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to design end-to-end supply chain security and runtime integrity for multi-cloud CNFs, including identity management, attestation mechanisms, policy-as-code enforcement, and network isolation during zero-downtime upgrades.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE/SPIRE identity management
- TPM/IMA runtime attestation
- SPDX SBOM delta validation
- OPA/Kyverno policy enforcement
- Cilium eBPF network policies
- Canary upgrade strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# SPIFFE identity configuration
apiVersion: spiffe.example/v1
kind: SPIFFEIdentity
metadata:
  name: cnf-identity-01
spec:
  spiffeID: spiffe://cluster/ns/cnf-01
  parentID: spiffe://cluster/ns/workload-scheduler
  ttl: 1h
```

```yaml
# OPA upgrade gate policy
package cnf.upgrade
default allow = false

allow {
  input.attestation.trust_score >= 80
  input.sbom.delta.additions == 0
  input.network_policy.isolated == true
}
```

## Implementation Approach
The solution integrates identity, attestation, and policy enforcement to ensure upgrades maintain security posture while achieving zero downtime through controlled canary deployments.

Keeps the implementation approachable for beginners while demonstrating proper boundary isolation between tenants.

- Tenancy isolation
- Sidecar-based request authorization
- Kubernetes ConfigMaps as a policy store
- Path and method matching
- Health and status endpoints

## Code Example
```javascript
// Policy format loaded from ConfigMap
{
  "tenantA": { "/api/v1/*": ["GET", "POST"], "allow": true },
  "tenantB": { "/api/v2/*": ["GET"], "allow": true }
}
```

**YAML Manifest (cnf-gateway-namespace.yaml)**:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-acl-policy
  namespace: cnf-gateway
data:
  cnf.acl.enabled: "true"
  cnf.acl.policy: |
    {
      "tenantA": {
        "/api/v1/*": ["GET", "POST"],
        "allow": true
      }
    }
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- ResourceQuota: Enforces aggregate resource limits across a namespace
- LimitRange: Defines default requests/limits and validates pod resource specifications
- Per-namespace isolation: Ensures tenants cannot exceed allocated resources
- Quota enforcement: Kubernetes rejects pods that would exceed quota limits
- Validation methods: kubectl describe quota and limitrange commands

## Code Example
```yaml
# Namespace: cnf-tenant-A
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A-quota
  namespace: cnf-tenant-A
spec:
  hard:
    limits.cpu: 4
    limits.memory: 16Gi
    requests.cpu: 2
    requests.memory: 8Gi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: cnf-tenant-A-limits
  namespace: cnf-tenant-A
spec:
  limits:
  - default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    type: Container
```
